name: Mitch Green

bio.statement: The City of Portland says Green was elected District 4 city councilor in November 2024 and began his term in January 2025.
bio.excerpt: Elected as City Councilor for District 4 in November 2024 and began their term of office in January 2025.

bio.statement: The Portland Mercury describes Green as a PhD economist, anti-war Army veteran and current District 4 councilor.
bio.excerpt: Green is a PhD economist, anti-war Army veteran, and a current District 4 councilor.

bio.statement: Green's voters' pamphlet statement lists prior governmental experience at the Bonneville Power Administration.

positions.statement: In his voters' pamphlet statement, Green says the biggest corporations should pay their fair share.
positions.excerpt: Make the biggest corporations pay their fair share

positions.statement: Green's pamphlet statement calls for creating permanently affordable housing.
Green's pamphlet statement calls for guaranteeing collective bargaining rights for tenants.
positions.excerpt: Guarantee collective bargaining rights for tenants

positions.statement: Green's pamphlet statement calls for using the Portland Clean Energy Fund for urgent climate resiliency.
positions.excerpt: Use Portland Clean Energy Fund for urgent climate resiliency

positions.statement: Green's pamphlet statement calls for funding evidence-based solutions to homelessness.
Green's pamphlet statement calls for lowering barriers to entry for street vendors and small businesses.
positions.excerpt: Lower barrier to entry for street vendors and small businesses

positions.statement: On his City of Portland council page, Green says the city has an opportunity to go big and build the public goods residents deserve.
positions.excerpt: We have the opportunity to go big and build the public goods that we deserve.

positions.statement: The Portland Mercury reports that since taking office Green has focused on holding fossil fuel companies accountable at the Critical Energy Infrastructure Hub.
positions.excerpt: Since taking office, he’s focused on holding fossil fuel companies accountable at the Critical Energy Infrastructure Hub

gaps: City filing form (AUD-120) text contained no candidate fields

collection_log.result: nothing relevant (council agendas, Wikipedia; press results duplicate step 5)

collection_notes: Steps run identically for all 12 District 4 candidates: (1) county Military & Overseas Online Voters' Guide statement PDF plus the City Auditor's AUD-120 candidate filing form (linked from portland.gov 2026 city candidates page); (2) portland.gov/council roster and councilor page for incumbents; (3) campaign domain only as printed in the pamphlet statement or filing form; (4) one general WebSearch; (5) three fixed allowed-domain WebSearch groups (opb.org+oregoncapitalchronicle.com+wweek.com+ballotpedia.org; kgw.com+koin.com+kptv.com+katu.com; portlandmercury.com+vote411.org+pamplinmedia.com+portlandtribune.com) because the search proxy rejects oregonlive.com and apnews.com; (6) the two articles that profile every District 4 candidate: OPB 'What to know about Portland's District 4 council race' (2026-10-07) and Portland Mercury 'Meet the Candidates For City Council District 4' (2026-09-11). Multi-winner race: OPB states three District 4 seats are on the ballot. Excerpts come through a summarizing fetch tool that limits verbatim quotes to ~125 characters, so some are fragments. Ballot name/order match inventory.json and the county Ballot Content RCV report. Incumbent per portland.gov/council (listed under District 4).
